summary: Antonio Terrone is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Leiden University under Tilmann Vetter and Barend J. ter Haar, also studying under traditional teachers, and served as scholar in residence at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

Antonio Vigilante works in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Bari (2009–2012) and has held teaching positions at Liceo Enea Silvio Piccolomini and the University of Siena (2025–2026).
Antonín Jan Jungmann (1775–1854) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He earned a Dr.med. from Charles University (1800–1805), where he later served as Professor of Medicine from 1808 to 1850.

Anuj Misra is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Cape Town and the University of Canterbury under Clemency Montelle and Kim Plofker, later holding posts at MPIWG, the University of Copenhagen, and the Free University of Berlin.

Anukul Chandra Banerjee (1911–1999) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned a PhD from the University of Calcutta, studying under Nalinaksha Dutt and Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya, and served as Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and professor at Calcutta.

Anupam Chakraborty works in Indology and other fields. He earned a BBA from the Bengal School of Technology and Management (2019–2022) and studied for an MBA at the Indian Institute of Engineering Science and Technology, Shibpur (2023–2025).
Anuradha Seneviratna (1938–2009) was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Peradeniya (~1961–1965) and later served there as a professor from circa 1984 to 2004.

Anushka Kahandagamage is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned degrees from the University of Colombo, South Asian University, and the University of Otago (PhD 2021–2024), and held a postdoctoral fellowship at Harvard University (2025–2026).
Anvita Abbi is a linguistics and Indology scholar. She studied at Cornell University (~1971–1975) and served on an editorial board at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1976–2013).
Aparajita Kundu is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. She received her PhD from Jadavpur University and serves as an Assistant Professor at Surendranath College.

Aram Frenkian (1898–1964) worked in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Alexandru Ioan Cuza University and the University of Bucharest (PhD), also training under Antoine Meillet, Theodor Bloch, and Louis Finot, and was a professor of Greek at Chernivtsi and Bucharest.

Archibald Campbell (1805–1874) was a scholar in Indology and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Glasgow, University of Edinburgh (Dr.med.), and Cambridge (M.A.), where he later served as Lecturer in Indian Law.

Archibald Campbell Carlleyle (1831–1897) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as curator at the Riddell Museum and as an assistant to Cunningham in the Archaeological Survey of India from 1871 to 1885.

Archibald Edward Gough (1845–1915) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Oxford under Monier Monier-Williams and held posts at Benares Sanskrit College, Presidency University, Aliah University, and the University of Allahabad.

Archie John Bahm (1907–1996) specialized in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Albion College and the University of Michigan, and held positions at Texas Tech, the University of Denver, and the University of New Mexico.

Arend Willem Mauritz Odé (1887–1951) was a linguist who earned his PhD from Leiden University and studied at the University of Copenhagen under Holger Pedersen and Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck. He worked as a teacher and conrector at Grotius College.
Arghyadip Mondal is a scholar in Buddhist studies, computational fields, and Indology. He is attested as a PhD researcher at Ghent University (2026).

Ariana Maki is a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology who completed her PhD at Ohio State University. She has held posts at the University of Colorado Boulder, the University of Idaho, and the University of Virginia.
Ariane Macdonald is a Tibetologist who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. She held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 1972) and succeeded Marcelle Lalou.
Arild Engelsen Ruud is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who earned his PhD at the London School of Economics (1991–1995). He was appointed Professor at the University of Oslo in 2007.
